answer.rationale: Verify the low-cost vendor’s onboarding and invoicing record, plus the prior second-source experience during a shortage. With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, switching entirely to a new primary could increase delivery risk despite meeting the spend mandate. A guarded second-source launch preserves incumbent continuity while testing whether the low-cost vendor can safely absorb volume; allocation and savings should remain provisional until capacity and delivery performance are demonstrated.
